final_text:
# Incident Report: GootLoader Infection — DESKTOP-H8ALZBV

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames). No IDS/Suricata alert export or other artifact was present in the evidence directory — this analysis is derived entirely from the packet capture via `tshark`.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC address | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org (DC: WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org, 10.8.15.4) |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** (observed in Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameStrings from 10.8.15.133) |
| OS / browser | Windows 10/11 x64, Microsoft Edge 127.0.2651.98 (from HTTP User-Agent strings) |

## Malware family: GootLoader

**Attribution basis: behavioral/TTP, not signature-confirmed.** No AV or IDS signature is present in the evidence to name the family directly. The call is based on reconstructing and deobfuscating the actual dropper code pulled from the capture, which matches GootLoader's well-documented, distinctive delivery technique:

- A ~6.99 MB JScript file (`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`) is padded with megabytes of scraped, legitimate-looking prose (excerpts from IPCC, OECD, and MPI technical/programming documents) wrapped in `/* ... */` block comments, with tiny real JScript statements interspersed between comment blocks — a purpose-built AV/size evasion technique specific to GootLoader.
- Stripping the comment blocks recovers the real logic: it string-concatenates `"WinHTTP.WinHTTPRequest.5.1"` and `"Object"` piece by piece, calls `WScript.CreateObject(...)` on it, issues a `GET` to a second attacker domain, calls `WScript.Sleep(10000)` (anti-sandbox delay), and then executes the fetched response body via `Function(responseText)()`. This staged fetch-and-eval handoff is the canonical GootLoader stage-1→stage-2 mechanism.

## Infection timeline (from packet timestamps)

| t+ (s) | Event |
|---|---|
| 74.68 | DNS resolves `quote.checkfedexexp.com`; victim `GET`s a ZIP disguised as a FedEx "quote" |
| 80.27 | 2.77 MB ZIP download completes, containing the padded `Invoice-...js` GootLoader dropper |
| 100.22–100.28 | DNS resolves `business.checkfedexexp.com`; TLS session opened (matches the WinHTTP stage-2 URL hardcoded in the decoded JS — traffic itself is encrypted) |
| 135.94–136.16 | `HEAD`/`GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` to raw IP **72.5.43.29** using a spoofed `Microsoft BITS/7.8` User-Agent (BITSAdmin abuse) — delivers a PE32+ x64 DLL |
| 196.86 → 1962.02 | Persistent HTTP beacon to **72.5.43.29:80**: 308 `GET`/`POST /` requests over ~30 minutes, fixed User-Agent `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the anomalous space before the version), carrying a large base64-style blob in the `Cookie` header as the tasking/exfil channel |

The secondary DLL payload (imports `WS2_32.dll`, `ole32.dll`, `advapi32.dll`; internal name `release.dll`) has no identifying family strings — it is referred to here only as the second-stage payload, not named as a specific commodity RAT/beacon, since the network evidence does not support that level of attribution.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — hardcoded C2 IP (never resolved via DNS), persistent beacon + secondary-payload host

**Malicious domains** (both Cloudflare-fronted; resolve to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159)
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com`
- `business.checkfedexexp.com`

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (stage-1 ZIP delivery)
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent=IxGTZjXqxJ&Jr_cid=9464552&L=817438388` (stage-2 fetch URL, recovered from the decoded JS; wire traffic is TLS-encrypted)
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (secondary DLL payload)
- `http://72.5.43.29/` (ongoing C2 beacon, GET and POST)

**Files and hashes**
| File | Description | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| (ZIP, no filename in HTTP response) | Stage-1 ZIP archive from `quote.checkfedexexp.com` | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | GootLoader stage-1 JS dropper (extracted from ZIP) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | Secondary-stage PE32+ x64 DLL fetched via BITSAdmin from 72.5.43.29 | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

## Recommendation

Isolate DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133) from the network immediately, reset the `plucero` account and any credentials cached on the host, and block `72.5.43.29`, `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, and `business.checkfedexexp.com` at the perimeter. Given GootLoader's history of leading to hands-on-keyboard follow-on activity, treat this as a compromise requiring full host reimage rather than simple malware removal.
